claims.text: The proposed alloy is equiatomic or near-equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
Rapid solidification will refine the initial grain structure of Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
Solution treatment at 1400°C for 20 minutes will dissolve ordered phases and homogenize Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
Water quenching after solution treatment will retain a supersaturated single-phase BCC Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr structure.
Aging at 600°C for 120 hours will produce discrete approximately 50 nm B2 precipitates in a continuous disordered BCC matrix.
The heat treatment will invert the microstructure from a continuous ordered B2 matrix with discrete BCC regions to a continuous BCC matrix with discrete B2 precipitates.
A continuous disordered BCC matrix permits dislocation mobility and plastic deformation, thereby improving ductility.
Discrete nanoscale ordered B2 precipitates impede dislocation motion and provide precipitation strengthening.
The B2 precipitates will be rich in Al, Zr, Hf, and Ti.
The processed Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy will have a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1300-1400 MPa.
The processed alloy will exhibit greater than 20% room-temperature compressive fracture strain.
The processed alloy will exhibit greater than 20% room-temperature tensile fracture strain.
The alloy density will be below 10 g/cm³.
Excluding tungsten will reduce density relative to W-based RHEAs.
As-cast Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys typically have a continuous ordered B2 matrix, yield strength above 2000 MPa, and ductility below 5%.
A continuous ordered B2 matrix is associated with high strength but low room-temperature ductility.
The approach requires the composition to form a single-phase BCC solid solution at 1400°C and then precipitate B2 during aging.
If aging instead produces a continuous B2 network, ductility will remain low.
The operating temperature must remain below the order-disorder transition temperature for B2 to remain stable.
The optimal aging kinetics and elemental partitioning for Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr may differ from those of Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr and have not been verified by the cited evidence.

contradictions.description: The proposed composition contains only Hf, Mo, Ta, Ti, and Zr, but the mechanism describes B2 precipitates as Al-rich even though no Al is present in the proposed alloy.
